items.headline: Fed holds at 3.75–4.00% in a 10–2 vote; two officials wanted a hike
items.summary: The chair said inflation is still elevated and declined to signal the next move; markets read hints of a December hike. As expected yesterday, but the dissents are new. Ongoing tightening bias.
items.rationale: A hawkish hold keeps US yields and the dollar firm, sustaining pressure on the rupee, G-Secs and foreign flows into India.

items.headline: Brent rises 1.3% to $115.32 as US reportedly tells Gulf states to prepare for post-election Iran strikes
items.summary: WTI gained nearly 3% to $102.78. Reversal after two days of easing; a strike on a Saudi refinery added to supply worries. Iran says it is still giving diplomacy a chance.
items.rationale: Crude back above $115 raises India's import bill, fuel-subsidy risk and inflation, and keeps pressure on the rupee and bonds.

items.headline: Iran says Hormuz could reopen within days if the US lifts its blockade and meets conditions
items.summary: Its foreign minister said reopening could beat the seven-day plan; conditions include lifting oil sanctions and freeing assets. Mediators push for a deal before the 3 November US vote. Ongoing diplomacy, unconfirmed timeline.
items.rationale: A reopening would be the biggest relief for Indian oil, LNG and freight costs, but US strike planning makes the outcome highly uncertain.

items.headline: Industrial output grows 6.7% in September, down from a revised 7.8% in August; mining shrinks 6.2%
items.summary: Manufacturing rose 7.6% and electricity 11.2%. Better than yesterday's 6% lender forecast but below a 7.3% poll. Motor vehicles and electrical equipment led. Slowing, not stalling.
items.rationale: Solid manufacturing supports earnings for autos and capital goods, while the slowdown and mining contraction hint that high oil and rates are starting to bite.

items.headline: Rupee falls 21 paise to 95.28 per dollar on a firmer dollar and higher crude
items.summary: It opened at 95.01 and touched 95.29. Reverses Tuesday's small gain. Pressure persists near record lows.
items.rationale: A weaker rupee raises imported oil and input costs and adds to inflation, while helping exporters' rupee earnings.

items.headline: RBI sold about $18.2 billion between 1 and 16 October to defend the rupee, its biggest this year
items.summary: Reserves have fallen to about $721 billion from a $785.7 billion peak in early September. Escalating defence as oil and outflows weigh.
items.rationale: Heavy dollar sales steady the rupee but drain reserves and rupee liquidity, which can push up short-term rates.

items.headline: Foreign investors buy a net ₹872 crore; domestic funds add ₹643 crore (provisional)
items.summary: A second day of foreign buying after ₹4,240 crore on Tuesday, though October outflows still exceed ₹48,000 crore. Tentative reversal.
items.rationale: Back-to-back foreign buying eases pressure on heavyweights and the rupee, but flows remain fragile with oil above $115.

items.headline: 10-year G-Sec yield trades 7.46–7.49%, near its highest since March 2023
items.summary: High oil after a Saudi refinery strike and expectations of more RBI tightening keep yields near multi-year highs. Ongoing.
items.rationale: Elevated yields raise borrowing costs for the government, companies and home buyers and pressure banks' bond books.

items.headline: SEBI member calls for more guardrails in derivatives trading to protect retail investors
items.summary: Remarks signal possible further curbs on futures and options. SEBI also extended a debenture-trustee compliance deadline to April 2027. New.
items.rationale: Tighter derivatives rules could cut trading volumes, weighing on exchanges, brokers and capital-market firms.
